name: Three ambient-piano melody devices: a vector melody (one-direction Dorian scale run that may start and end on a dissonant 9th/11th), a classical sequence (a short phrase stepped down one scale degree at a time over chords that all keep one common tone in the bass), and modal transformation (two chord tones slip up a half step, maj7 -> min7 -> maj7, and the melody switches Lydian -> Dorian -> Lydian while the harmony keeps rising)
goal: Write ambient melodies that tell a story without wobble or randomness, using three named devices from the source: (1) VECTOR melody: a plain scale run in one direction (down, up, or horizontal as a repeated two-note figure), e.g. E Dorian descending over Em6 -> Em7 inner-voice motion, allowed to start on the 9th (F#) and end on the 11th (A) because the motion justifies the dissonance; repeat it from a new start note over a new chord (e.g. from high A over an A chord) and return. (2) SEQUENCE: a short melodic ornament repeated one scale degree lower each time, over chords that share one bass tone placed on the offbeat (A under Dm/A -> Am7 -> Bbmaj7 -> A augmented -> A7, which resolves to D in the next section). (3) MODAL TRANSFORMATION (neo-Riemannian-style common-tone moves): Gbmaj7 with a Gb Lydian melody -> slip two notes up a half step to Gm7 (Bb and F stay) and play G Dorian -> slip its 3rd and 7th up a half step to Gmaj7 and play G Lydian -> keep going (Am7 -> Amaj7), adjusting the melody to each new mode.

source.title: 3 Simple Tricks for Beautiful Ambient Melodies

prerequisites: A DAW or notation tool with a piano and a soft pad underneath, plus reverb
Basic chord spelling (root/3rd/5th/7th) and mode knowledge (Dorian = minor with raised 6th, Lydian = major with raised 4th)

inputs.name: tempo
inputs.description: Slow tempo; the source plays rubato/slow

outputs.name: melody_clips
outputs.description: One MIDI clip per device: vector, sequence, modal transformation

outputs.name: chord_map
outputs.description: Chord spelling per bar showing common tones and the half-step slips

constraints: Pitch stays steady: no pitch bends, glides or random notes; all motion is written note-by-note (Matt's preference).
Dissonant start/end notes (9th, 11th) are fine inside a vector melody because the line is clearly moving; do not park on them over a static bar.
Sequence: same phrase shape, each repeat one scale step lower (diatonic, not chromatic); keep the shared bass tone on the offbeat.
Modal transformation: exactly two chord tones move by a half step per change; the other two are held as common tones. Re-fit the melody to the new mode at every change.
Original piano/pad sounds; not affiliated with any piano library vendor named in the source.
Ableton/MIDI-friendly: device names map to stock Live devices or generic modules; patterns are plain MIDI clips.
If the track has drums, they enter early (~8 counts / ~10-12 s); only pad/texture before that (Matt's preference).

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Set up the accompaniment: a repeating E minor pattern whose only change is one inner voice moving a step (Em6 -> Em7, C# -> D). Put a quiet pad under the piano and add reverb.
steps.expect: Gentle, almost static bed with interior motion

steps.action: Vector melody: play a simple E Dorian scale descending over the bed. Try starting it on the 9th (F#) and ending on the 11th (A) so it begins and ends on bitey tones (Em69 colour).
steps.expect: A one-direction line that feels purposeful despite the dissonant ends

steps.action: Repeat the same scale shape from a new start note over a new chord (e.g. from high A over an A chord instead of E minor), then return to where you started.
steps.expect: Hook from repeated direction, new colour from the new chord

steps.action: Sequence: write a short melodic ornament (a few notes) and repeat it, moving it down one scale degree each time, two or three times.
steps.expect: A recognisable phrase stepping down through the scale

steps.action: Under the sequence, keep one common tone in the bass on the offbeat: Dm with A in the bass -> Am7 -> Bbmaj7 (A is its major 7th) -> A augmented -> A7 (the two upper notes step down). Let A7 (V of D) resolve to D at the next section.
steps.expect: Moving harmony glued by a held A, ending on a dominant that resolves

steps.action: Modal transformation: play Gbmaj7 (Gb Bb Db F) with a Gb Lydian melody (raised 4th, C).
Slip two notes up a half step (Gb -> G, Db -> D; Bb and F stay) to get Gm7, and re-fit the melody to G Dorian.
steps.expect: Same melody shape, darker new mode, smooth voice leading

steps.action: Now slip Gm7's 3rd and 7th up a half step (Bb -> B, F -> F#) to get Gmaj7, and play G Lydian. Continue the climb the same way (Am7 -> Amaj7 by raising the 3rd and 7th), adjusting the melody each time.
steps.expect: Constantly rising harmony with new colours from the same simple phrase

verification: Vector clip: melody notes are monotonic in one direction (or a repeated two-note horizontal figure) and use only E Dorian pitch classes.
Sequence clip: each repeat has the same interval pattern as the first, transposed down one diatonic step; every chord in the sequence contains the bass pitch class A.

Modal clip: consecutive chords differ by exactly two pitch classes, each moved by one semitone (Gbmaj7 -> Gm7 -> Gmaj7 -> ... ); melody notes over each chord fit the stated mode (Lydian over maj7, Dorian over min7).
No pitch-bend or glide events in any clip.
